about: The 12 finalists for Keshav to judge, second version (after ChatGPT's cross-check, 1 Nov 2026). Chosen from 55 captured sites to be radically different from each other, clean and premium as Keshav asked, still original, and with quality that survives without a celebrity, an expensive product or a campaign budget. Frames are file names inside each site's folder.

finalists.name: Immersive Garden
finalists.idea: Your cursor raises a white plaster relief out of a quiet page.

finalists.name: Making Software
finalists.idea: A technical manual: one blueprint drawing language on white.

finalists.name: Non-Objective: Time
finalists.idea: Hundreds of hand-drawn clocks, each a different idea of time.

finalists.name: Teenage Engineering
finalists.idea: One object under a spotlight; its long shadow becomes a dry joke.

finalists.name: OXMAN
finalists.idea: A research lab with authority: claim, team, specimen, number.

finalists.name: Rauno Freiberg
finalists.idea: A sideways strip of exact white cards; Swiss restraint with one yellow.

finalists.name: Radio Garden
finalists.idea: Two colours; the globe made of live stations is the whole interface.

finalists.name: Kenta Toshikura
finalists.idea: Black and white; every project seen through one circular portal.

finalists.name: Henry Heffernan
finalists.idea: An engineer's portfolio as a computer on a desk that you actually use.

finalists.name: Igloo Inc.
finalists.idea: One material, ice, held through the whole scroll film.

finalists.name: Nothin'
finalists.idea: A giant black wordmark on white, broken by one sculpted figure.

finalists.name: Odd Works
finalists.idea: An exact grid carrying genuinely playful objects.

cut_from_version_1.why: ChatGPT: the reveal's power comes from a famous face and a racing helmet; take those away and it is a standard mask effect. Claude agrees.
ChatGPT: the quality is a photogenic product and expensive staging; Making Software already carries the technical-drawing idea. Claude agrees.
ChatGPT: a benchmark for execution backed by a campaign budget, not a transferable personal identity. Claude agrees.

ChatGPT: a nostalgic company fiction would be costume on an individual; Henry Heffernan covers complete fictions. Claude partly disagrees (the boot-screen loader is the best answer to the loader problem) and keeps it as the first alternate.
ChatGPT: its first frame is blank, which contradicts our own first-frame rule. Claude agrees; kept as a case-study layout reference.
